title: Lure of the Golden Deer
introduction: On spotting the deer Seetha calls Rama and Lakshmana to have sight of it. Lakshmana immediately concludes it to be Maareecha, but Seetha, keeping his observation aside asks Rama to fetch it. Rama is also fascinated when he looked at that deer and he explains to Lakshmana as to why that particular deer is to be hunted down.
closing: Poor Seetha, she could not romanticise the Golden Deer better than Rama. Then it may be asked 'what is the necessity for Rama to romanticise and compare it to the skyey star-deer and others. Is it for the deer or for the deerskin?' This is the unanswered question. 'It is for the deer alone but not its skin,' said so in reply by some. If it were to be for the deerskin, from the view point of Rama, he could have shot his arrow from where he is standing, which arrow miraculously pierces any terrain, kills the deer, and safely comes back into his quiver, as in the case of showing his prowess to Sugreeva. Otherwise, Rama should have turned down the request of Seetha, as he did in the ninth chapter of this Aranya Kanda, when she was saying: 'where that weapon? Where this forest? Where the principles of Kshatriya? And where is the sageness? All this is inconsistent... By us, let the laws of the land be esteemed...' as at 3-9-27. When kings come into such a sort of allurement, many wise men quote this instance of Rama's going after the deer as a reminder to them, as in Maha Bharata.
"Impossible is the birth of a Golden Deer, even then Rama is lured, if time is perilous, even the best man's brain deranges.'
Fate harasses the faculty, faculty cannot harass the fate, even the cleverest Rama, went after the Golden Deer.
Unborn it was, none has seen yet, nor mentioned about it, such is the mirage of Rama. Parlous time causes perilous percipience.

Hence Rama's going after the deer is for the deerskin, on one count, and for the deer itself, on the other as affirmed by Lakshmana because Lakshmana never says untruth. This Maareecha is recurrently falling after Rama. Once an accident, twice a coincidence, but thrice... a habituation... and it become habitual for Maareecha to dare Rama. Hence, Rama has to do something to Maareecha, permanently.

The other view according to puranic/mythological sayings is that god endows whatever you seek. But that god alone says: 'Seek you will get it, but seek not by the extrinsic values of objects.' This saying has it counterpart at: 'Every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth.' St Matthew, p[Ch. 7, v. 8] The Bible. But 'seek something within the nature, according to your nature... but not the supernatural... for eyes belie the nature of objects...' is the essence here. He/she who seeks beyond means will have to suffer, either by getting it or devoid of it. This is said in innuendo at 3-43-33, that 'the results of pipedreams fill the coffers of Shukra.'

Further, because parlous time has come to Rama and Seetha, epically, providentially, and episodically, Rama has to move away from Seetha. While going after the deer, Rama says much to Lakshmana about the security to Seetha and also informs him that 'she is pivotal to our mission.' He did not say these many farewells when sending Seetha and Lakshmana for hiding in a cave at the time of elimination Khara, Duushana, and the other fourteen thousand demons. At one time Rama spared Maareecha's life in the forest of Tataka while guarding Vishwamitra's ritual, only to cause Maareecha to come now. As such, Rama has to go after Maareecha. Besides, Seetha or Goddess Lakshmi will let none killed in her presence.
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे त्रि चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 43rd chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
सा तम् संप्रेक्ष्य सुश्रोणी कुसुमानि विचिन्वती |
हेम राजत वर्णाभ्याम् पार्श्वाभ्याम् उपशोभितम्
प्रहृष्टा च अनवद्यान्गी मृष्ट हाटक वर्णिनी |
भर्तारम् अपि च आक्रन्द लक्ष्मणम् चैव सायुधम्
verses.iast:
sā tam samprekṣya suśroṇī kusumāni vicinvatī |
hema rājata var.hṇābhyām pār.hśvābhyām upaśobhitam
prahṛṣṭā ca anavadyāngī mṛṣṭa hāṭaka varṇinī |
bhartāram api ca ākranda lakṣmaṇam caiva sāyudham
verses.translation: That slender-waisted Seetha whose limbs are flawless, whose complexion is like purified gold, and who is presently culling flowers is highly gladdened to observe the Golden Deer that is brightened in one flank with the colour of gold and the other is silvery, and she shouted for attention of her husband, and even that of Lakshmana who is presently weaponed.

glosses.meaning: purified, gold, one in colour of - complexioned one
with golden, silver, tinged, with flanks
[who is] with, weapon, at Lakshmana, also thus

verses.devanagari:
आहूय आहूय च पुनः तम् मृगम् साधु वीक्षते |
आगच्छ आगच्छ शीघ्रम् वै आर्यपुत्र सह अनुज
verses.iast:
āhūya āhūya ca punaḥ tam mṛgam sādhu vīkśate |
āgaccha āgaccha śīghram vai āryaputra saha anuja
verses.translation: "Oh, noble prince, come here," thus she called her husband and peered at the deer, and again she called, "really come with your younger brother quickly," and again gazed at the deer, and thus she oftentimes called and oftentimes saw the deer fondly.

glosses.meaning: with, younger brother, quickly, come here, really
again [oftentimes,] at that, deer, fondly, gazing.

verses.devanagari:
तया आहूतौ नरव्याघ्रौ वैदेह्या राम लक्ष्मणौ |
वीक्षमाणौ तु तम् देशम् तदा ददृशतुः मृगम्
verses.iast:
tayā āhūtau naravyāghrau vaidehyā rāma lakṣmaṇau |
vīkṣamāṇau tu tam deśam tadā dadṛśatuḥ mṛgam
verses.translation: Those manly lions Rama and Lakshmana thus bidden by Vaidehi came there exploring that place and then they saw that Golden Deer.

glosses.meaning: bidden, manly, lions [vyaahra also means lion]

verses.devanagari:
शंकमानः तु तम् दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणो रामम् अब्रवीत् |
तम् एव एनम् अहम् मन्ये मारीचम् राक्षसम् मृगम्
verses.iast:
śaṃkamānaḥ tu tam dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇo rāmam abravīt |
tam eva enam aham manye mārīcam rākṣasam mṛgam
verses.translation: But Lakshmana became incredulous on seeing it and said to Rama, "I believe this deer to be that Maareecha, the demon."

glosses.meaning: becoming incredulous, Lakshmana, on his part
him, as Maareecha, demon, alone, I believe.

verses.devanagari:
चरन्तो मृगयाम् हृष्टाः पापेन उपाधिना वने |
अनेन निहता राम राजानः काम रूपिणा
verses.iast:
caranto mṛgayām hṛṣṭāḥ pāpena upādhinā vane |
anena nihatā rāma rājānaḥ kāma rūpiṇā
verses.translation: "Oh, Rama, when kings engaged in hunting games were delightedly moving in the forest, this Maareecha killed many of them resorting to many disguises, for he is a guise-changer by his wish.

glosses.meaning: delightedly, in game of hunting, who are moving around, kings

verses.devanagari:
अस्य मायाविदो माया मृग रूपम् इदम् कृतम् |
भानुमत् पुरुषव्याघ्र गन्धर्व पुर संनिभम्
verses.iast:
asya māyāvido māyā mṛga rūpam idam kṛtam |
bhānumat puruṣavyāghra gandharva pura saṃnibham
verses.translation: "Maareecha is an expert in many wiles and he has now assumed the form of this Golden-Deer, oh, manly lion, which is not more than the scintillating city of Gandharva-s, a city of wiles, which any trickster can create to make-believe.
notes: The 'Gandharva-city' is the name given to a make-believe formation of a city-like structure in skies by magicians, and presently the magicians world over are making the apparent structures to disappear, rather than constructing one which is un-manifest.

glosses.meaning: this, wily, Golden-Deer, form, is made - he assumed.

verses.devanagari:
मृगो हि एवम् विधो रत्न विचित्रो न अस्ति राघव |
जगत्याम् जगतीनाथ माया एषा हि न संशयः
verses.iast:
mṛgo hi evam vidho ratna vicitro na asti rāghava |
jagatyām jagatīnātha māyā eṣā hi na saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, Raghava, this kind of amazing animal with gemlike dapples is nonexistent in the world, isn't it. Hence, oh, lord of the world, this is truly a phantasm. No doubt about it." So said Lakshmana to Rama.
notes: Here the timely provision of data by Lakshmana may be noticed. Rama is also aware of it, but Lakshmana is reminding him. Lakshmana cites even the name of Maareecha and by this, we can infer as to why Ravana chose Maareecha for this particular purpose. Because Maareecha has that extraordinary ability to lure and has a good record of wily accomplishments, Ravana chose him. Lakshmana has done his duty in presenting expedient data and it is up to Rama to analyse it. Rama argues on this point later in the chapter.

glosses.meaning: oh, world/earth, lord of, [such a] Raghava
in world, non, existent, isn't it

verses.devanagari:
एवम् ब्रुवाणम् काकुत्स्थम् प्रतिवार्य शुचि स्मिता |
उवाच सीता संहृष्टा चद्मना हृत चेतना
verses.iast:
evam bruvāṇam kākutstham prativārya śuci smitā |
uvāca sītā saṃhṛṣṭā cadmanā hṛta cetanā
verses.translation: While Lakshmana of Kakutstha-s is speaking thus, she who is self-satisfied as her heart is conjured by the cozenage, such a Seetha of a toothy smile deterred him and spoke.

glosses.meaning: one with whitely, smile - with a toothy smile
this way, who is speaking, Kakutstha Lakshmana
in turn, on forestalling - on deterring

verses.devanagari:
आर्यपुत्र अभिरामो असौ मृगो हरति मे मनः |
आनय एनम् महाबाहो क्रीडार्थम् नः भविष्यति
verses.iast:
āryaputra abhirāmo asau mṛgo harati me manaḥ |
ānaya enam mahābāho krīḍārtham naḥ bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: "Oh, nobleman's son, that delightful deer is stealing my heart, oh, dextrous one, bring it round, it will be our plaything.

glosses.meaning: for us, for playing, [a plaything,] it will become.

verses.devanagari:
इह आश्रम पदे अस्माकम् बहवः पुण्य दर्शनाः |
मृगाः चरन्ति सहिताः चमराः सृमराः तथा
verses.iast:
iha āśrama pade asmākam bahavaḥ puṇya darśanāḥ |
mṛgāḥ caranti sahitāḥ camarāḥ sṛmarāḥ tathā
verses.translation: "Here in the threshold of our hermitage many animals with adorable manifestation are moving about in flocks and herds, say Caamara deer, like that Srimara deer.
notes: The cāmara is the kind of deer of species Bos grunniens and śrimara is a larger variety than chaamara.

glosses.meaning: of ours, here, in hermitage's, threshold
collectively - in flocks and herds, move about.

verses.devanagari:
ऋक्षाः पृषत संघाः च वानराः किनराः तथा |
विचरन्ति महाबाहो रूप श्रेष्ठा महाबलाः
verses.iast:
ṛkṣāḥ pṛṣata saṃghāḥ ca vānarāḥ kinarāḥ tathā |
vicaranti mahābāho rūpa śreṣṭhā mahābalāḥ
verses.translation: "Also the animals that are excellent in their form, say monkeys, are moving here. Likewise herds of Kinnara deer, spotted-deer, and even bears of great-might are freely moving here.
notes: Here the Kinnaraa-s are another kind of deer and not to be confounded with yaksha, gandharva, kinnaraa celestials.

verses.devanagari:
न च अस्य सदृशो राजन् दृष्ट पूर्वो मृगः मया |
तेजसा क्षमया दीप्त्या यथा अयम् मृग सत्तमः
verses.iast:
na ca asya sadṛśo rājan dṛṣṭa pūrvo mṛgaḥ mayā |
tejasā kṣamayā dīptyā yathā ayam mṛga sattamaḥ
verses.translation: "As to how this extraordinary deer is appearing, oh, king, by way of its brilliance, tameness, or by the lustre of its skin, I have not so far seen any coequal to this.

glosses.meaning: as to how it is appearing
by brilliance, by meekness [tameness,] by lustre [of skin]
by me, not seen, earlier - so far.

verses.devanagari:
नाना वर्ण विचित्र अंगो रत्न भूतो मम अग्रतः |
द्योतयन् वनम् अव्यग्रम् शोभते शशि संनिभः
verses.iast:
nānā varṇa vicitra aṃgo ratna bhūto mama agrataḥ |
dyotayan vanam avyagram śobhate śaśi saṃnibhaḥ
verses.translation: "Diversely coloured, amazingly limbed, and spotted with gemlike dapples it is shining forth like a deer that is completely gemmy, and while nonchalantly moving before me it is enlivening the forest like the moon.

verses.devanagari:
अहो रूपम् अहो लक्ष्मीः स्वर संपत् च शोभना |
मृगो अद्भुतो विचित्रांगो हृदयम् हरति इव मे
verses.iast:
aho rūpam aho lakṣmīḥ svara sampat ca śobhanā |
mṛgo adbhuto vicitrāṃgo hṛdayam harati iva me
verses.translation: "Ah, what a form, ah, what a brilliance, what a beautiful bleat! This amazingly limbed deer is wonderful, and this is stealing my heart, as it were.

glosses.meaning: ah, [what a] form, ah, [what a] brilliance
my, heart, stealing, as it were.

verses.devanagari:
यदि ग्रहणम् अभ्येति जीवन् एव मृगः तव |
आश्चर्य भूतम् भवति विस्मयम् जनयिष्यति
verses.iast:
yadi grahaṇam abhyeti jīvan eva mṛgaḥ tava |
āścarya bhūtam bhavati vismayam janayiṣyati
verses.translation: "It will be surprising if this deer draws into your capture alive and well, as it creates astonishment to one and all.

verses.devanagari:
समाप्त वन वासानाम् राज्य स्थानाम् च नः पुनः |
अंतःपुरे विभूषार्थो मृग एष भविष्यति
verses.iast:
samāpta vana vāsānām rājya sthānām ca naḥ punaḥ |
aṃtaḥpure vibhūṣārtho mṛga eṣa bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: "When we return to kingdom on completing our dwelling in forest this deer becomes a masterpiece in palace-chambers for us.

glosses.meaning: for us - on completing, forest, dwelling
again, in kingdom, when [we will be] staying, also
in palace-chambers, decoration, for the sake of - as a masterpiece

verses.devanagari:
भरतस्य आर्यपुत्रस्य श्वश्रूणाम् मम च प्रभो |
मृग रूपम् इदम् दिव्यम् विस्मयम् जनयिष्यति
verses.iast:
bharatasya āryaputrasya śvaśrūṇām mama ca prabho |
mṛga rūpam idam divyam vismayam janayiṣyati
verses.translation: "Oh, lord, the form of this deer creates an excellent jubilation to Bharata, to you the son of the nobleman, to my mothers-in-law, and also to me in palace-chambers.

verses.devanagari:
जीवन् न यदि ते अभ्येति ग्रहणम् मृग सत्तमः |
अजिनम् नरशार्दूल रुचिरम् तु भविष्यति
verses.iast:
jīvan na yadi te abhyeti grahaṇam mṛga sattamaḥ |
ajinam naraśārdūla ruciram tu bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: "Else if that best deer does not come into you capture while alive, oh tigerly-man, at the least its gorgeous deerskin will be remnant of it.

glosses.meaning: into your, capture, no, comes into, else if
beautiful, deerskin, on its part, will be there - will be remnant with us.

verses.devanagari:
निहतस्य अस्य सत्त्वस्य जांबूनदमय त्वचि |
शष्प बृस्याम् विनीतायाम् इच्छामि अहम् उपासितुम्
verses.iast:
nihatasya asya sattvasya jāmbūnadamaya tvaci |
śaṣpa bṛsyām vinītāyām icchāmi aham upāsitum
verses.translation: "I wish to sit along with you on its golden deerskin, overlaying it on a seat of tender darbha grass-blades, in case the deer is felled.
notes: The seat of those that are under a vow is called bR^isii, vratiinaam aasanam bR^isii, ajina, carma, kR^ittiH : amara kosha 'A seat covered with darbha, the sacred grass, [and if available] a deerskin thereon.'

glosses.meaning: tender darbha grass-blades, on seat of
killed, that, being's - of that killed deer
in golden, skin - on the deerskin

verses.devanagari:
कामवृत्तम् इदम् रौद्रम् स्त्रीणाम् असदृशम् मतम् |
वपुषा तु अस्य सत्त्वस्य विस्मयो जनितो मम
verses.iast:
kāmavṛttam idam raudram strīṇām asadṛśam matam |
vapuṣā tu asya sattvasya vismayo janito mama
verses.translation: "Tradition says that this sort of unruly self-seeking is unbefitting to women, yet that deer's beautiful body is inducing curiosity in me." Seetha said so to Rama and remained waiting for his reply.
notes: Seetha talked only this much and left the fulfilment of her indent to the discretion of Rama. There is neither demand nor compulsion to bring the deer in her talk. But we usually hear the telltale stories, bringing from some other texts, which say that Seetha pestered, nagged, and harassed Rama to get this deer. But nothing of that sort is evident from the dialogue given to her by Valmiki. She started to ask Rama with a suchiH smitaH 'a white smile, i.e., a toothy smile or a simpering smile' that too to deride the security guard, namely Lakshmana. These security personnel all over the world and in all situations and always forewarn the secured, and on the other hand, it is customary to the secured person to jump off the cordon of security, disdainful of the security measures. After all, human nature wants a free living. Thus, when Seetha is trying to jump off the cordon of security laid by Lakshmana, commentators say that she is said to have smiled scornfully.lakśmaṇa vākya śravaṇa janita kopā sītā rāmam eva āha - dk'with the anger generated on listening Lakshmana's words, Seetha spoke to Rama,' Whether Seetha is with kopa 'anger' or not, it is unsaid in the text.

glosses.meaning: this sort of, independent behaviour - self-seeking
to me, astonishment - curiosity, is induced.

verses.devanagari:
तेन कांचन रोम्णा तु मणि प्रवर शृंगिणा |
तरुण आदित्य वर्णेन नक्षत्र पथ वर्चसा
बभूव राघवस्य अपि मनो विस्मयम् आगतम् |
verses.iast:
tena kāṃcana romṇā tu maṇi pravara śṛṃgiṇā |
taruṇa āditya varṇena nakṣatra patha varcasā
babhūva rāghavasya api mano vismayam āgatam |
verses.translation: As for that deer's horns they vie with excellent sapphires, its golden coat with the glitter of tender sun, and its ambience with silver spots on coat with a milk way containing twinkling stars, and by that reason even Raghava's heart is awestruck when he saw it.
notes: According to this original text, Rama is more lured by the Golden Deer than Seetha, whereas later legends made Seetha a scapegoat. Rama too did not fancifully come under the lure but he got his own logistics to fall after the deer, which we come across in the following speeches of Rama. The word api 'even,' is a normal metrical filler at most times, but assumes importance at times. Here Rama is the all knowing and all deciding personality as depicted until now, and 'even' he is lured by the deer, say Maareecha's supernal trickery.

glosses.meaning: stars, pathway [milky way,] having resplendence - ambience
by that reason, on its part

verses.devanagari:
एवम् सीता वचः श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा च मृगम् अद्भुतम्
लोबितः तेन रूपेण सीताया च प्रचोदितः |
उवाच राघवो हृष्टो भ्रातरम् लक्ष्मणम् वचः
verses.iast:
evam sītā vacaḥ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā ca mṛgam adbhutam
lobitaḥ tena rūpeṇa sītāyā ca pracoditaḥ |
uvāca rāghavo hṛṣṭo bhrātaram lakṣmaṇam vacaḥ
verses.translation: In this way, hearing the words of Seetha and observing that wondrous deer Raghava is also amused by its form, and even motivated by Seetha in fetching it, he delightedly spoke this word to his brother Lakshmana.
notes: When Seetha placed her indent before Rama, Rama is speaking to Lakshmana, only to allow us to listen his strategy in going after the deer. atra mṛgayā vyasana doṣān jānan api rāmo - lobhitaḥ ten rūpeṇa - iti anayo uktayā mahā purusānatra mṛgayā vyasana doṣān jānan api rāmo - lobhitaḥ ten rūpeṇa - iti anayo uktayā mahā puru//sānām api bhavati vyasana anurūpatayā buddhi vyāmoho bhavati iti sūcitam - dk -

'here knowing well about the blemishes of hunting games, Rama is lured, ambitioned, hankered after etc. By these words it is suggested that even great people are beguiled for their inclination in such matters - Dharmaakuutam;

asambhave hemamayasya jantoḥ tathā api rāmo lulubhe mṛgāya | sabhā parva - bhārata - rāmo hema mṛgam na vetti - - - dyūte bhrātṛ catuṣṭayam ca mahiṣīm dharmātmajo dattavān | prāyaḥ sat puruṣo hi anartha samaye buddhyā parityajyate - - prācīnā

'even if it is impossible to have a golden deer, Rama is lured by it for his hunting game' Maha Bharata, sabhaa parva ; 'Rama, unable to distinguish illusory deer [went after it...] Yudhistar staked all his four brothers and his queen [in dice game...] thus even great people at inopportune times loose their brains,' an ancient saying.

glosses.meaning: in this way, Seetha's, words, on hearing
wondrous one, [that] deer, having observed, also

verses.devanagari:
पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेह्याः स्पृहाम् उल्लसिताम् इमाम् |
रूप श्रेष्ठतया हि एष मृगो अद्य न भविष्यति
न वने नंदनोद्देशे न चैत्ररथ संश्रये |
कुतः पृथिव्याम् सौमित्रे यो अस्य कश्चित् समो मृगः
verses.iast:
paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehyāḥ spṛhām ullasitām imām |
rūpa śreṣṭhatayā hi eṣa mṛgo adya na bhaviṣyati
na vane naṃdanoddeśe na caitraratha saṃśraye |
kutaḥ pṛthivyām saumitre yo asya kaścit samo mṛgaḥ
verses.translation: "Lakshmana, behold this enthusiastic delight of Vaidehi. Oh, Soumitri, presently no other deer indeed with such an excellent form exists in this forest. Or else, does it exist in Nandana Gardens of Indra - no, it cannot be there; in the adjoins of Caitraratha Gardens of Kubera - no, it will not be there, then how can there be some deer on earth which is similar to this!

glosses.meaning: Vaidehi's, enthused, this, delight, you see
presently, by form's, by excellence, for sure
on earth, how - how can there be.

verses.devanagari:
प्रतिलोम अनुलोमाः च रुचिरा रोम राजयः |
शोभन्ते मृगम् आश्रित्य चित्राः कनक बिन्दुभिः
verses.iast:
pratiloma anulomāḥ ca rucirā roma rājayaḥ |
śobhante mṛgam āśritya citrāḥ kanaka bindubhiḥ
verses.translation: "Amazing are its hairlines with hair upturned at some places and down-turned at other, and the golden spots embedded on the coat of the deer are glittery.

glosses.meaning: deer, abiding - embedded [on coat of deer,] are glittery.

verses.devanagari:
पश्य अस्य जृंभमाणस्य दीप्ताम् अग्नि शिखोपमाम् |
जिह्वाम् मुखात् निःसरंतीम् मेघात् इव शत ह्रदाम्
verses.iast:
paśya asya jṛmbhamāṇasya dīptām agni śikhopamām |
jihvām mukhāt niḥsaraṃtīm meghāt iva śata hradām
verses.translation: "See at its tongue that is exserting from its mouth while it is yawning, which is similar to the flaring tongue of fire and to the lightning from a cloud.

glosses.meaning: while yawning, from its, from mouth
flaring, fire, crests - tongue of fire, similar, at tongue
in hundred ways, which is flowing - lightning

verses.devanagari:
मसार गल्वर्क मुखः शंख मुक्ता निभ उदरः |
कस्य नाम अनिरूप्यः असौ न मनो लोभयेत् मृगः
verses.iast:
masāra galvarka mukhaḥ śaṃkha muk{}tā nibha udaraḥ |
kasya nāma anirūpyaḥ asau na mano lobhayet mṛgaḥ
verses.translation: "Its face is like a mug made up of sapphires, its paunch is pearly and conchoidal, and whose heart is it that will not lured for this deer with an inexplicable beauty.

glosses.meaning: whose, in name, heart, not, lures.

verses.devanagari:
कस्य रूपम् इदम् दृष्ट्वा जांबूनदमय प्रभम् |
नाना रत्नमयम् दिव्यम् न मनो विस्मयम् व्रजेत्
verses.iast:
kasya rūpam idam dṛṣṭvā jāmbūnadamaya prabham |
nānā ratnamayam divyam na mano vismayam vrajet
verses.translation: "On seeing at this astounding look of the deer which is golden in glitter and bejewelled numerously as it were, whose heart is it that will not be transported into astonishment.

glosses.meaning: whose, mind, into astonishment, not, transported.

verses.devanagari:
मांस हेतोः अपि मृगान् विहारार्थम् च धन्विनः |
घ्नन्ति लक्ष्मण राजानो मृगयायाम् महावने
verses.iast:
māṃsa hetoḥ api mṛgān vihārārtham ca dhanvinaḥ |
ghnanti lakṣmaṇa rājāno mṛgayāyām mahāvane
verses.translation: "Kings pursuing games of hunting in great forests, oh, Lakshmana, will be felling deer either for the sake of flesh, or just for the purpose of sporting archery.

glosses.meaning: kings, in great, forests, in games of hunting
flesh, for the sake of, even
archers [of bows, or, to use bows in sport, archery]

verses.devanagari:
धनानि व्यवसायेन विचीयन्ते महावने |
धातवो विविधाः च अपि मणि रत्न सुवर्णिनः
verses.iast:
dhanāni vyavasāyena vicīyante mahāvane |
dhātavo vividhāḥ ca api maṇi ratna suvarṇinaḥ
verses.translation: "And exerting themselves in great forests they by far amass forest produce, ores, jewels, gemstones and the gravel of gold.
notes: 'And this deer is also the produce of this forest, as such hunting this for taming or tanning is befitting to us, as we are princes.' One should not 'exert oneself,' or 'amass' forest produce even if he is a king, but collect it casually without looting it.

glosses.meaning: by far, they will be amassing.

verses.devanagari:
तत् सारम् अखिलम् नॄणाम् धनम् निचय वर्धनम् |
मनसा चिन्तितम् सर्वम् यथा शुक्रस्य लक्ष्मण
verses.iast:
tat sāram akhilam nṝṇām dhanam nicaya vardhanam |
manasā cintitam sarvam yathā śukrasya lakṣmaṇa
verses.translation: "Everything of that wealth from forest produce will be filling the treasuries of kings, like the speculated objects filling the entire treasury of Shukra just by his thinking of them in his mind.
notes: Whatever object Shukra thinks wilfully, it becomes a reality, filling his treasury. So also, whatever objects the kings desire they come to reality through forest produce. This is a puranic/ legendary saying which Rama is quoting.

Or, as contained in Maha Bharata, Udyoga Parva, Suparna-Narada discourse: manuṣyebhya samādatte śukraḥ cintā ārjitam dhanam 'the pipedreams, [the unattainable or fanciful hopes or schemes,] of people fill up the coffers of Shukra.'

Or, dhaninām kośa vardhanam dhanam sāram 'for rich people [like kings, merchants,] coffer, filling, wealth, i.e., the forest produce is the best.' 'The forest produce is the best wealth for enriching the coffers of the kings for maintenance of kingdom, and for other rich people it is for trade etc.' Hence, this deer, or its deerskin is sāram 'an excellent gift' to be taken to Ayodhya on our return.' Rama's saying is interpreted in this way giving a high priority to forest produce.

glosses.meaning: in mind, that which is thought

verses.devanagari:
अर्थी येन अर्थ कृत्येन संव्रजति अविचारयन् |
तम् अर्थम् अर्थ शास्त्रज्ञः प्राहुः अर्थ्याः च लक्ष्मण
verses.iast:
arthī yena artha kṛtyena saṃvrajati avicārayan |
tam artham artha śāstraGYaḥ prāhuḥ arthyāḥ ca lakṣmaṇa
verses.translation: "The financial experts and the other financially well-off people say that with which aspirational activity an aspirant unhesitatingly scurries and achieves it, that achieved target alone is lauded to be worthwhile, or, as real wealth.
notes: To support his argument that bringing the Golden Deer shall not become a pipedream but it shall occur in reality, Rama is substantiating with this statement. This is called apūrva vastu sekaraṇa 'collection of valuable objects' which is a fashion to anyone, especially to kings. Then Lakshmana may further insist 'even then you shall not go, it is a fanciful deer/demon,' for which Rama is saying 'getting the un-gettable itself is worthwhile.'

glosses.meaning: finance, science, knowers of - financial experts
who have reaped riches, financially-well people
they - well, say, well-said - lauded by them.

verses.devanagari:
एतस्य मृग रत्नस्य परार्ध्ये कांचन त्वचि |
उपवेक्ष्यति वैदेही मया सह सुमध्यमा
verses.iast:
etasya mṛga ratnasya parārdhye kāṃcana tvaci |
upavekṣyati vaidehī mayā saha sumadhyamā
verses.translation: "This comely Vaidehi will be sitting on that invaluable golden skin of that gem of a deer along with me.
notes: Rama is not primarily bothered to tame the Golden Deer by declaring about its skin and its usage at this juncture. This skin alone is the 'laudable wealth' 'worthwhile object' and a 'masterpiece.'

glosses.meaning: that this [such a,], deer, gem of a

verses.devanagari:
न कादली न प्रियकी न प्रवेणी न च अविकी |
भवेत् एतस्य सदृशी स्पर्शनेन इति मे मतिः
verses.iast:
na kādalī na priyakī na praveṇī na ca avikī |
bhavet etasya sadṛśī spar.hśanena iti me matiḥ
verses.translation: "I think the skin of Kadali deer, or of Priyaki deer, or of Praveni deer, or as a matter of fact the skins of best breed of deer or sheep will not be match to the deerskin of this deer, insofar as the soft-touch is concerned.
notes: Kadali, Priaki and Avi are the names of breed of deer that yield best deerskins. It is said in amara kośa: kadalī kandalī cīnaḥ ca camūru priyakaḥ; amī ajina yonayaḥ; avayaḥ śaila meṣa arka Kadali is the deer with white stripes on its neck that lives in a big burrows. Priyaki will have thick brown and black hair and these yield the best and soft deerskin for sitting. AviH is the sheep in breed. The word Praveni may perhaps not of a breed of deer as said in amara kosha: aiṇeya meṇyāḥ carmādyameṇaḥ aiṇam ubhe triṣu Thus it conveys the meaning aiNeya, the best deer belonging to doe, and aiNa, belonging to buck. Some take this praveNi as a separate breed whose dictionary meaning is completely different than that of deer.

glosses.meaning: by way of [soft-] touch of skin - now assessed by seeing
to this, matching, not, it becomes

verses.devanagari:
एष चैव मृगः श्रीमान् यः च दिव्यो नभः चरः |
उभौ एतौ मृगौ दिव्यौ तारामृग महीमृगौ
verses.iast:
eṣa caiva mṛgaḥ śrīmān yaḥ ca divyo nabhaḥ caraḥ |
ubhau etau mṛgau divyau tārāmṛga mahīmṛgau
verses.translation: "Only two divine deer are there, this magnificent deer on earth, and the other that moves in skies remaining in stellar region.
notes: The deer in skies is taken in two ways; one, the deer in the moon and the other, the Orion constellation, mṛga śīrṣa, mṛga śira 'deer, as its head,' i.e., the deer-like stars in the head of Orion, where East takes this Orion as the 'hunted' and West takes it as the 'hunter', in which 'hunting' is common. And Rama wants to hunt down the reality of the deer. But Lakshmana may still insist saying, 'maybe, only these two deer are the unavailable objects. We cannot leap up to skies to catch hold of those deer-like stars, or the deer in the moon. Equally this tricky deer on earth is uncatchable. Thereby getting its skin is also that dreamy.' For this Rama explains his duty in his next course of action, viz., killing the demon.

glosses.meaning: magnificent one, this, deer, also, thus
in stars, deer - in stellar region, i.e., in Orion or in moon

verses.devanagari:
यदि वा अयम् तथा यत् माम् भवेत् वदसि लक्ष्मण |
माया एषा राक्षसस्य इति कर्तव्यो अस्य वधो मया
verses.iast:
yadi vā ayam tathā yat mām bhavet vadasi lakṣmaṇa |
māyā eṣā rākṣasasya iti kartavyo asya vadho mayā
verses.translation: "You are telling me that 'this is the wizardry of the demon.' Even then, Lakshmana, if this results in that way as a demon's wizardry, my duty also results in the elimination of that deer.

glosses.meaning: that way, this, results in, [wizardry of demon]
if, else - even then - if he is a demon
by me, its [deer/ demon's,] killing, is the duty [that results in

verses.devanagari:
एतेन हि नृशंसेन मारीचेन अकृत आत्मना |
वने विचरता पूर्वम् हिंसिता मुनि पुंगवाः
verses.iast:
etena hi nṛśaṃsena mārīcena akṛta ātmanā |
vane vicaratā pūrvam hiṃsitā muni puṃgavāḥ
verses.translation: "If this deer is Maareecha, this heinous and vicious-souled demon has indeed tortured many eminent sages earlier when was on the prowl in the forests, thus he is eliminable.

glosses.meaning: if this is Maareecha, by him]

verses.devanagari:
उत्थाय बहवो अनेन मृगयायाम् जनाधिपाः |
निहताः परम इष्वासाः तस्मात् वध्यः तु अयम् मृगः
verses.iast:
utthāya bahavo anena mṛgayāyām janādhipāḥ |
nihatāḥ parama iṣvāsāḥ tasmāt vadhyaḥ tu ayam mṛgaḥ
verses.translation: "He rebelliously killed many kings who are excellent archers while they were in hunting games, at least for that reason this bestial monster is eradicable.
notes: The last word in second foot mṛga is also identifiable with 'beast' thus a bestial monster.

verses.devanagari:
पुरस्तात् इह वातापिः परिभूय तपस्विनः |
उदरस्थो द्विजान् हन्ति स्व गर्भो अश्वतरीम् इव
verses.iast:
purastāt iha vātāpiḥ paribhūya tapasvinaḥ |
udarastho dvijān hanti sva garbho aśvatarīm iva
verses.translation: "Demon Vaataapi who held ascetics in contempt was here earlier, and staying in the stomachs of Brahmans he used to come out by ripping their stomachs open and thus he was killing Brahmans, like a mare-calf killing its own mother at its time of birth by ripping the womb of its own mother.
notes: The legend of Vaataapi is said in detail in chapter 11 of this Aranya Kanda when Rama and others were going to Agastya's hermitage.

verses.devanagari:
स कदाचित् चिरात् लोभात् आससाद महामुनिम् |
अगस्त्यम् तेजसा युक्तम् भक्ष्यः तस्य बभूव ह
verses.iast:
sa kadācit cirāt lobhāt āsasāda mahāmunim |
agastyam tejasā yuk{}tam bhakṣyaḥ tasya babhūva ha
verses.translation: "On one occasion after some time, that Vaataapi avariciously obtained that great-saint and the one who is endowed with effulgent, namely Agastya, as an eatable, but actually that demon has became an eatable to the sage.

glosses.meaning: an eatable, he became - demon became

verses.devanagari:
समुत्थाने च तत् रूपम् कर्तु कामम् समीक्ष्य तम् |
उत्स्मयित्वा तु भगवान् वातापिम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
samutthāne ca tat rūpam kartu kāmam samīkṣya tam |
utsmayitvā tu bhagavān vātāpim idam abravīt
verses.translation: "On observing the demon Vaataapi who is trying to assume his original form of demon in order to come out of his stomach, that godly saint Agastya spoke this to Vaataapi with a scornful smile.

glosses.meaning: in the matter of getting up - demon's coming out from the stomach of the sage
that, aspect, [demon's aspect,] to make [when trying to renew demon's form,] when demon was intending to
god - godly saint Agastya, on observing
him [at demon,] [with a scornful] smile, but

verses.devanagari:
त्वया अविगण्य वातापे परिभूताः च तेजसा |
जीव लोके द्विज श्रेष्ठाः तस्मात् असि जराम् गतः
verses.iast:
tvayā avigaṇya vātāpe paribhūtāḥ ca tejasā |
jīva loke dvija śreṣṭhāḥ tasmāt asi jarām gataḥ
verses.translation: " 'Oh, Vaataapi, you have irreverently eradicated the best Brahmans in this world owing to your might, therefore I have assimilated you.' So said sage Agastya to Vaataapi.

glosses.meaning: somatic, world - on earth, in this world
a vi gaNya = not, verily, counting - without taking into account - disregarding irreverently
therefore, into digestion, gone, you are you are digested by me.

verses.devanagari:
तत् एतत् न भवेत् रक्षो वातापिः इव लक्ष्मण |
मत् विधम् यो अतिमन्येत धर्म नित्यम् जितेन्द्रियम्
भवेत् हतो अयम् वातापिः अगस्त्येन इव मा गतः |
verses.iast:
tat etat na bhavet rakṣo vātāpiḥ iva lakṣmaṇa |
mat vidham yo atimanyeta dharma nityam jitendriyam
bhavet hato ayam vātāpiḥ agastyena iva mā gataḥ |
verses.translation: "Lakshmana, such a demon who is like Vaataapi will not be there any more. He who disregards someone of my kind, who always abides in righteousness and who is self-controlled, such a demon will be eliminated as sage Agastya has eliminated demon Vaataapi, if that demon happens to get at me.

glosses.meaning: righteousness, one who is always abiding
one who is of my, kind of
he, me, on getting at [confronting, if he provokes]

verses.devanagari:
इह त्वम् भव संनद्धो यंत्रितो रक्ष मैथिलीम्
अस्याम् आयत्तम् अस्माकम् यत् कृत्यम् रघुनंदन |
verses.iast:
iha tvam bhava saṃnaddho yaṃtrito rakṣa maithilīm
asyām āyattam asmākam yat kṛtyam raghunaṃdana |
verses.translation: "Oh, Lakshmana, the descendent of Raghu, you stay here in all preparedness and guard Maithili steadfastly, whatever enterprise of ours is there that is founded in her.
notes: The first foot 'she is the basis of our mission' is a debated expression. Their mission is to eliminate Ravana. Seetha as Vedavati, an earlier incarnation of Goddess Lakshmi, vows to eliminate Ravana when she comes to earth as Seetha. Then Rama should have said 'look Lakshmana, our task is to kill Ravana, for that Ravana has to kidnap Seetha, and to make that kidnapping possible do not guard her.' Can he say so? Neither Rama, nor any ordinary husband can say so. Then this predictive sentence becomes self-contrary. Contrariwise, taking some concessions of grammar, because most of Ramayana is un-Paninian, Rama is indirectly hinting Lakshmana that something is immanent, because 'after the elimination of demons like Khara, Duushana nothing drastic has happened, but a queer deer has come, and thus something may now happen.' Then, if this asyāmis given to kartavyam'the enterprise' as tasmin then the connection is: asmākam yat kṛtyam asyām [tasmin] āyattam asāma'for us, which, enterprise is there, in that, circumspect, we shall be' 'Which enterprise is there for us individually, in that we both shall conduct separately and circumspectly, and you do your job of guarding Seetha and I mine in bringing the deer or its skin, duly eliminating that conjuring demon.' In such a case, the blemish soothsaying or prophesising will not occur to Rama, in saying 'Seetha as the pivotal character is to be kidnapped by Ravana' etc. In fact, Rama is the person who is more beguiled by the deer.

glosses.meaning: you, here, preparedly, you be [stay here]
= of our, which, enterprise is there

verses.devanagari:
अहम् एनम् वधिष्यामि ग्रहीष्यामि अथवा मृगम्
यावत् गच्छामि सौमित्रे मृगम् आनयितुम् द्रुतम् |
verses.iast:
aham enam vadhiṣyāmi grahīṣyāmi athavā mṛgam
yāvat gacchāmi saumitre mṛgam ānayitum drutam |
verses.translation: "I wish to catch this deer, Soumitri, if not I will kill it, and I will be going forthwith to fetch the deer.

glosses.meaning: I wish to catch, I, this, deer, athavaa = if not

verses.devanagari:
पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेहीम् मृग त्वचि गताम् स्पृहाम्
त्वचा प्रधानया हि एष मृगो अद्य न भविष्यति |
verses.iast:
paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehīm mṛga tvaci gatām spṛhām
tvacā pradhānayā hi eṣa mṛgo adya na bhaviṣyati |
verses.translation: "Lakshmana, see how Vaidehi's percept is overtaken by deerskin. Indeed by the strangeness of its skin that deer must be a mysterious being, hence, it will not survive now.

glosses.meaning: on deer, skin, reached [overtaken by,] one with such a percept
= by distinctiveness of [strangeness of,] deerskin, indeed
this, deer, now, not, will be there - survives.

verses.devanagari:
अप्रमत्तेन ते भाव्यम् आश्रमस्थेन सीतया
यावत् पृषतम् एकेन सायकेन निहन्मि अहम् |
हत्वा एतत् चर्म च आदाय शीघ्रम् एष्यामि लक्ष्मण
verses.iast:
apramattena te bhāvyam āśramasthena sītayā
yāvat pṛṣatam ekena sāyakena nihanmi aham |
hatvā etat carma ca ādāya śīghram eṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa
verses.translation: "Oh, Lakshmana, apply yourself vigilantly while staying in hermitage along with Seetha. So soon as I go I will be felling that spotted deer with one arrow and returning quickly.
notes: The ambiguity is whether Rama is going for the deer, or deerskin, or for the latent demon. He is going for the deer epically, for the memento of deerskin to Seetha as a hero of the epic, and for the demon in deer, according to mythology.

glosses.meaning: on killing, that, skin, also, on taking

verses.devanagari:
प्रदक्षिणेन अतिबलेन पक्षिणा
जटायुषा बुद्धिमता च लक्ष्मण |
भव अप्रमत्तः प्रतिगृह्य मैथिलीम्
प्रति क्षणम् सर्वत एव शन्कितः
verses.iast:
pradakṣiṇena atibalena pakṣiṇā
jaṭāyuṣā buddhimatā ca lakṣmaṇa |
bhava apramattaḥ pratigṛhya maithilīm
prati kṣaṇam sarvata eva śankitaḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, Lakshmana, you be here taking care of Maithili along with the forthright, formidable and fatherly bird Jatayu, and be watchful and suspicious from everywhere and every split-second." Thus Rama spoke to Lakshmana and started to go after the deer...

glosses.meaning: with sagacious [fatherly bird,] with Jatayu, also
